# Use mermaid-render

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Check Mermaid diagrams for the mistakes that stop them rendering (unknown diagram type, unbalanced brackets or quotes, unquoted parentheses in labels, the word end as a node id, missing arrows, unclosed subgraphs or alt blocks) with line numbers and a fix for each, then render them to SVG, PNG or PDF with mermaid-cli, or to a standalone HTML page when it is not installed. Works on a .mmd file or every mermaid fence in a Markdown doc.

**Reach for it when** a diagram "won't render", the user says "check my mermaid", "export this diagram as SVG/PNG", or needs the diagrams in a doc as image files.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install mermaid-render                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install mermaid-render --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install mermaid-render --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Converters pack: [`--pack converters`](../packs/use-the-converters-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/converters/skills/mermaid-render/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "My mermaid diagram says syntax error, can you find what's wrong?"
- "Export the diagrams in design.md as PNGs for my slides"
- "Check every mermaid block in this doc renders before I open the PR"
- "Convert arch.mmd to an SVG"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Draw an architecture diagram of our three-tier AWS app"
- "Turn design.md into an HTML page I can email"
- "Make design.md a Word document with the diagrams in it"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use mermaid-render".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every error has a line number and a fix,** in the user's file, not in a temporary copy.
- **Fixes keep the meaning.** Same nodes, same edges, same labels; only syntax changes.
- **Clean diagrams pass.** The `architecture-diagrams` examples and templates lint clean, and lint never blocks a diagram Mermaid itself accepts.
- **The output format matches the use:** SVG for documents, PNG for slides and chat.
- **Network dependence is stated.** The HTML fallback is named as needing network, with the install line for real files.

## Use something else when

- Drawing a new diagram from a description; use `architecture-diagrams`
- Converting the whole Markdown doc to a web page; use `md-to-html` (render the diagrams here first if readers are offline)
- Converting the whole doc to Word; use `md-to-docx`
